finalText:
Root cause: **double rounding**. `engine.js` rounded intermediate USD to 2 decimals mid-chain, then rounded again after FX conversion.

Percent coupon leaves sub-cent residual. `2 × $9.99 = 19.98`, minus 10% = `17.982`. Engine threw away `0.002` before converting. Rate then amplifies the loss, and when the converted residual straddles the `.005` boundary, final cent flips down.

Why "most look fine" — bug needs three things at once:
- **Percent coupon present.** Flat-only stays exact (2-dec minus whole 5), so `FLAT5` alone always passed.
- **Rate that amplifies past a boundary.** USD rate 1 too small to matter; EUR 0.9 happens to land same side. GBP 0.78, CAD 1.35 flip.
- **Right basket.** JPY only broke on `2×$10.04`, not `2×$9.99`.

10 of 40 matrix cases failed. All off by exactly one minor unit, always low (never over-charging):

| case | was | should be |
|---|---|---|
| GBP + SAVE10PCT, 2×$9.99 | 14.02 | 14.03 |
| CAD + SAVE10PCT+FLAT5, 2×$9.99 | 17.52 | 17.53 |
| JPY + SAVE10PCT, 2×$10.04 | 2692 | 2693 |

Stacking is not itself broken — flat just carries forward the error percent already made. Stack combos fail wherever percent-alone fails, same delta.

Fix applied in `src/pricing/engine.js:23-32`: keep full precision through discount chain, round once at end in target currency's decimals. 40/40 pass.

Separate issue, not covered by tests: `flat` has no clamp at zero. `FLAT15` on a basket under $15 yields a negative total.
